text:
Predicates:
WorksOnCampus(x) ::: x works in student jobs on campus.
OrderTakeout(x) ::: x orders takeout frequently in college.
EnjoysDiningHall(x) ::: x enjoys the dining hall meals and recipes.
PickyEater(x) ::: x is a picky eater.
SpendsTimeEating(x) ::: x spends a lot of their time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
Hannah(x) ::: x is Hannah.
AtSchool(x) ::: x is at Mary's school.
NeedsMoney(x) ::: x needs to earn money to help pay for college tuition.

Premises:
∀x (WorksOnCampus(x) → NeedsMoney(x)) ::: If people at Mary's school work in student jobs on campus, then they need to earn money to help pay for their college tuition.
∀x (OrderTakeout(x) → WorksOnCampus(x)) ::: If people at Mary's school order takeout frequently in college, then they work in student jobs on campus.
∀x (OrderTakeout(x) ∨ (EnjoysDiningHall(x) ∧ ¬PickyEater(x))) ::: People at Mary's school order takeout frequently in college or enjoy the dining hall meals and recipes.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHall(x) → ¬PickyEater(x)) ::: If people at Mary's school enjoy the dining hall meals and recipes, then they are not picky eaters.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHall(x) → (SpendsTimeEating(x) ∧ ∀y (SpendsTimeEating(y) → y spends a lot of their time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls))) ::: If people at Mary's school enjoy the dining hall meals and recipes, then they spend a lot of their time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
Hannah(atMarysSchool) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school.
∀x (Hannah(x) ∧ NeedsMoney(x)) → (¬PickyEater(x) ∧ NeedsMoney(x)) ::: If Hannah is at Mary's school and needs to earn money, then she is not a picky eater and needs to earn money to help pay for her college tuition.

Conclusion:
Hannah(atMarysSchool) ∧ ¬PickyEater(Hannah) ∧ SpendsTimeEating(Hannah) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school, she is not a picky eater, and spends a lot of her time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
